items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: And Bill later on made the arrangement for Basie. And I worked out a deal for Bill to be on the recording date... I had to get a marriage between the record companies. And I got that deal going... And Bill eventually missed the date, but Basie made the record anyway.

ctx.x: So we did the recording at Nola Studio. And I had had this hassle with him about that bass. I knew he wasn't getting enough bass on those recordings. So I found out that the bass was coming out at the bottom, and the treble was coming out up there further. I got ahold of the A&R man, who was a German; he'd just come to the... And he did... Everywhere I told him to put a mike, he put it. So I told him to put that mike down there and catch the bass... And Bill Jennings made the arrangement. So we recorded it. And…

And Bill later on made the arrangement for Basie. And I worked out a deal for Bill to be on the recording date. He was down in Atlantic City. I had to go through all kinds of jazz, because, see, Bill is one record label and Basie is on another. So I had to get a marriage between the record companies. And I got that deal going... And Bill eventually missed the date, but Basie made the record anyway. And Basie kind of outshone Bill.
